lyrics:
[Intro: lone harmonica, fingerpicked acoustic guitar]

[Verse 1: raw cracked male voice, close and dry]
You left with the truck running, mad as July
Said this town was a jar with the lid screwed tight
I said some things too. I was tired. I was wrong.
I've been changing that bulb ever since you've been gone

[Chorus: voice lifts and strains, fiddle joins]
There's a porch light yellow at the end of this road
It don't ask where you've been, don't say I told you so
The moths all know it, and the dog does too
Porch light yellow, burning for you

[Verse 2: guitar and soft kick drum]
Your mama says give it time, says you're just like me
Stubborn as a fence post, quiet as a tree
I see your friends at the feed store, they don't know what to say
I buy bulbs by the dozen. I got plenty. I can wait.

[Chorus: fiddle and harmonica together]
There's a porch light yellow at the end of this road
It don't ask where you've been, don't say I told you so
The moths all know it, and the dog does too
Porch light yellow, burning for you

[Bridge: voice and harmonica only, almost spoken]
If the sun comes up and you ain't in the drive
I shut it off for the day, to save the light
And I turn it back on when the sky goes gray
That ain't hope. It's just what I do. Every day.

[Final Chorus: full band, voice breaking on the last line]
There's a porch light yellow at the end of this road
It don't ask where you've been, don't say I told you so
The moths all know it, and the dog does too
Porch light yellow
Come on home, kid. It's on for you.

[Outro: harmonica alone, a screen door, tires on gravel]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 84 BPM, 3/4, E minor. A slow waltz with a lot of air in it, like a man talking to a road.

VOICE: Male tenor, rough and unpolished, cracking when he pushes into the chorus. Close and dry, with breaths left in. The bridge is nearly spoken. No harmonies until the last chorus, and then only one, low.

INSTRUMENTS: Fingerpicked acoustic guitar, harmonica, a single fiddle, a soft kick drum and brushed snare from verse 2, upright bass. Screen door and gravel sounds at the end.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, harmonica and guitar. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:50 Chorus 1, fiddle in. 1:20 Verse 2. 1:54 Chorus 2. 2:24 Bridge, voice and harmonica. 2:50 Final chorus, full band. 3:16 Outro, harmonica, a door, tires on gravel at 3:26.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Recorded like a live take in a wooden room: no gloss, a little tape noise, the voice louder than anything else.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The crack in his voice on 'burning for you' at 1:14.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man begging a lover to come back. This is the older one, the parent, who has stopped arguing with the sky and simply keeps a light on. The tires on gravel at the end are left unexplained.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Regret, stubborn waiting, routine as love, a car in the drive.
